messages:
sam: heads-up — proposal to change admit behavior for short peaky bursts in eu-west. instead of hard rejects when GPU queues blow past 30s, try a graceful downgrade path (decrease model size / force short responses) and only reject when both queue + fallback fail. thoughts?
maria: can you sketch the fallback chain? curious about cost/regression risk if we switch to smaller models during spikes.
sam: quick sketch: primary = r-instruct-13b (gpu-optimized), fallback1 = r-13b-quant (lower mem, slightly worse q), fallback2 = r-7b-int8 (fast, cheaper), final = reject 429. also option to cap max_tokens to 256 on fallbacks. aim is to keep p99 latency under SLO while avoiding big reject spikes for paying customers.
joel: +1 on concept. two questions: 1) how do we handle stateful chat KV cache when we switch models? 2) networking — if region is limited by egress, smaller models help but still like to know packet/backpressure behaviour.
sam: for KV we plan to attach a model-compatibility tag and only allow fallback if caller's session is stateless or session flagged allow-degrade. otherwise prefer queue or reject. for egress, degrade reduces average tokens generated so should lower egress. but we still need to watch burst-concurrency which hits GPU memory more than egress.
anita: concerned about eval/regression alerts. if we auto-degrade per customer, how do we ensure we don't silently worsen quality? we should tie degradations to a canary fraction and fire quality regressions to the eval pipeline.
sketch snippet i proposed (for runtime config):
```
admit_policy:
  max_queue_ms: 25000
  allow_degrade: true
  degrade_chain:
    - model: r-13b-quant
      max_tokens: 256
    - model: r-7b-int8
      max_tokens: 128
  final_action: reject
  metrics_tags: ["degrade", "auto-fallback"]
```
joel: looks fine. we need a per-sku override so enterprise customers can opt-out of degrade and always queue/reject. also rate-limit signals should incorporate remaining capacity across warmpool + burst buffer, not just node queue length.
kyle: operational note — our warm pool for eu-west is down 2x GPU due to a maintenance window tonight; if we flip admit policy now we'll see fallbacks more often. recommend delaying rollout until warmpool restored or reduce threshold to 15s for tonight only.
sam: good catch. delaying makes sense. alternative is to roll canary to 5% with explicit label "warmpool-degraded" so we can measure.
maria: for cost modeling, can we have a quick sim? degrade path reduces token cost by ~40-60% per request but may increase request count if users retry after degraded outputs. need to model retry behavior — maybe add retry-hint header so clients can avoid blind retries.
anita: +1 on retry-hint. also add audit log entry when degrade occurs so success teams can surface to customers.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary update initiated: admit-policy v2 -> eu-west-1 @ 5% traffic by sam at 2318532540. monitor: admit.policy.degrade_events, admit.policy.rejects, model.q-regress.alerts.
sam: thanks infra-bot. i'll hold full rollout until warmpool back. i'll also add a short-runbook for SRE: how to revert degrade (set allow_degrade=false) and how to pin fallback model.
joel: +1. can we add a temporary metric for "kv-incompatible-degrades" so we can see sessions that couldn't fallback due to state?
kyle: created ticket INF-4729 to refill warmpool tonight and to add per-sku opt-out. linking here: https://ourboard/INF-4729
maria: ok. next actions: sam to push canary config, anita to wire eval gating, joel to add kv-incompat metric, kyle to update warmpool ticket. aim to reassess in tomorrow's 10:00 sync if warmpool still down. :thumbsup:
